newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Profits up at Sweden's Assa Abloy lockmaker.
newsitem.headline: Profits up at Sweden's Assa Abloy lockmaker.

text.p: Swedish lockmaker Assa Abloy Friday posted a 63 percent jump in pre-tax profits for 1996 and said it saw continued good results in 1997.

Assa Abloy, the world's largest lockmaker, reported a pre-tax profit of 345 million crowns ($46.5 million) for the 12 months ending Dec. 31, 1996, compared with 212 million crowns ($28.6 million) in 1995.
Sales surged 43 percent in 1996 to 5.01 billion crowns ($675 million), with increased growth in the Nordic markets and Britain, reasonable growth in the United States and stable volumes in Germany.

Assa Abloy said a key event in 1996 was the acquisition of Essex of the United States, which has annual revenues of $243 million. It said Essex's unit for electronic hotel locks, System 45, was integrated with VingCard and its McKinney/Parker unit for bathroom accessories was divested.
